objective: Make partial review expressible in the M0 review-epoch model, so an honest partial review stops forcing a choice between a misdated record and a fabricated one.
falsifiable_claim: The claim fails if a reviewer who materially reviews a strict subset of the divergent entry set can still only produce an epoch that either (a) dates their review to an earlier epoch's date, or (b) stamps entries they did not review with their review date.
in_scope: Per-entry reviewed_as_of independent of whole-set epoch dating, or an equivalent delta-epoch that names only the entries it actually covers.
A recorded distinction between MATERIAL review and MECHANICAL unchanged-confirmation, so both are expressible and neither is misreported as the other.
Migration of the existing epoch chain to the new shape without rewriting historical attestations.

SAME-DATE SECOND CLOSE. The anchor cannot represent two closes on one date. Verified live before scoping: m0-program-control-model.mjs:4385 refuses a second entry sharing an epoch_id, the attestation binds the anchor head's epoch_id to the lock's current epoch id, and the lock partitions entries by reviewed_as_of (epochByDate, :4875-4897) so two same-date epochs would each claim the identical entry set. A within-date re-close therefore requires REWRITING the head entry, which check-attestation-chain now refuses -- correctly. The three escapes all falsify something: rewriting the head, minting a distinct id that breaks the attestation binding, or re-dating to a day the review did not happen.

PER-ENTRY reviewed_as_of, independent of whole-set epoch dating. This is the same model coarseness from the other side: because the epoch is the unit of dating, every baseline-divergent entry is forced onto the latest epoch date, so an honest partial review must either misdate itself or stamp entries nobody reviewed. Per-entry review provenance resolves BOTH faces -- the same-date impossibility and the forced-restamping -- which is why they are one record and one fix.
out_of_scope: Re-reviewing historical entries to satisfy the new shape.
Weakening the requirement that a divergent entry binds a review.

aggregate_disposition.why: Owner ruling 2026-08-02. This is a TOOL defect exposed by the M5 review-fix census, not an M0 exit claim. M0 already exited with open-successor holds; binding this would reopen a certified stage to fix an ergonomics-of-attestation problem. It is filed so the defect is owned and dated rather than worked around in every future census.

implementation_actions: Add per-entry review dating, or delta-epochs that enumerate their own covered set.
Introduce an explicit mechanical-unchanged-confirmation state distinct from material review.
Assert both in the M0 self-test with predeclared rejections.
positive_proof: A reviewer covering a strict subset of the divergent set produces an epoch whose covered set equals exactly what they reviewed, dated to when they reviewed it.
Mechanical unchanged-confirmation and material review are distinguishable in the recorded artifact, and a consumer can tell which was performed for any given entry.
adversarial_or_fault_proof: Reject an epoch that claims coverage of an entry the reviewer neither materially reviewed nor mechanically confirmed.
Reject a review recorded under a date on which it did not occur, including the case where an earlier epoch is extended across a date boundary to avoid forcing the whole divergent set onto a new date.

Reject a second close on a date the chain already carries: today it is unrepresentable, and the record's own rule is that nothing which cannot be represented truthfully gets represented. The fix must make it representable, not permitted-by-exception.

Reject a per-entry dating scheme that lets an entry carry a review date without a corresponding recorded review -- per-entry dating widens what can be stated, and the widening must not become a place to state review that did not occur.
remaining_nonclaims: This record does not claim the existing epoch chain is wrong; it claims the chain cannot express partial review without a false statement somewhere.
This record does not claim any specific past attestation was fabricated.
rollback_or_stop_rule: Stop if per-entry dating cannot preserve the existing chain's integrity guarantees; a weaker chain is worse than an awkward one.
current_implementation_evidence: FILED 2026-08-02 from the M5 review-fix census. The tool forces every entry divergent from the immutable comparison baseline to bind the LATEST epoch date. Measured at that census: appending an epoch for the actual review date would have forced 675 entries onto it, of which 559 (js-outbound, js-host-action, dev-replay-action, service) were never touched by the cut. The implementer refused to append on those grounds, and the owner accepted the refusal but rejected extending a prior epoch across a date boundary as equally false. The resolution for that census was to do the review the attestation claims -- mechanical unchanged-confirmation for the untouched set -- which is correct but does not scale as a general answer. The defect is that the model has no way to say 'this epoch covers these entries, reviewed this way, on this date', so every honest partial review must either misdate itself or over-claim. That is a tool making truthful records impossible, and it gets fixed at the tool. SCOPE ADDED 2026-08-04 (queue item 3), with both gaps BYTE-VERIFIED STILL OPEN before scoping rather than assumed from the earlier encounter -- the standing constraint after R-12 proved a register can trail the tree, and absence is the harder claim. GAP 1 (same-date second close) hit live during the M5 closing round: appending a second anchor entry for 2026-08-03 SUCCEEDED and M0 then refused with 'review anchor sequence 32 duplicates an anchored epoch'. The attempt was reverted, not forced, and the owner ruled the ORDER wrong and the CHAIN right -- entry review implies an epoch append, artifact refresh does not. GAP 2 (whole-set dating) was measured at 1430 forced entries of which 559 were never touched by the cut that would have stamped them. Both faces are one model defect and take one fix: per-entry review provenance.
compatibility_and_migration: The existing chain is migrated, never rewritten; historical attestations keep their recorded scope.
